body:
I think the problem here is inside the `JoltPhysicsDirectSpaceState3D::body_test_motion` function and not inside Jolt. I've updated the MRP to make it more minimal and to bring it straight to the frame where it breaks:

[test-angled-ceiling-collision.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26388100/test-angled-ceiling-collision.zip)

Edit `character_body_3d.gd` and comment out these 2 lines if you want the capsule to slide towards the collision again:

```
position = Vector3(5.806422, 1.249025, 0.0)			# <---- These 2 lines force the capsule to the bad frame, comment out to see full movement
velocity_avg = Vector3(-4.375038, -1.149564, 0.0)		# <----
```

The `JoltPhysicsDirectSpaceState3D::body_test_motion` will first do some collision tests to recover the capsule out of collision. This doesn't seem to cause any issues. Then it will call this:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4a919adccf8e398aceca75399c539078c54fe97f/modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_physics_direct_space_state_3d.cpp#L887

This will find a hit with the ceiling and return:

```
hit = true
safe_fraction = 0
unsafe_fraction = 6.10351562e-05
```

Then it executes:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4a919adccf8e398aceca75399c539078c54fe97f/modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_physics_direct_space_state_3d.cpp#L892

Note that `scale` is not passed to this function, so if there is any I think we have a bug. Scale is `(1 1 1)` for this example so this is not causing an issue here. Inside the function it will find a single hit with the ceiling (same hit as in the previous function) and it will proceed with that hit until:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4a919adccf8e398aceca75399c539078c54fe97f/modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_physics_direct_space_state_3d.cpp#L342-L343

```
normal = (0.254129, -0.96717, 0)
direction = (-0.96717, -0.254129, 0)
```

resulting in `direction.dot(normal) == 0` and the function earlying out and returning that there is no collision. This in turn causes the capsule to move into the floor and things are broken. Note that it is no coincidence that the direction is perpendicular to the normal because the GDScript does `velocity_avg = velocity_avg.slide(normal_to_handle)` to make it so.

If I change the code to:

```
if (direction.dot(normal) >= CMP_EPSILON) {
	continue;
}
```

it doesn't early out anymore and the capsule no longer goes into the floor. 

I find it dangerous that the code that bisects collision to get the safe and unsafe fraction uses a different condition for detecting a collision than the code that retreives the contact information. This can lead to completely ignoring a collision as we can see in this case. If this condition is needed, I would say it is needed in both functions (and should probably be made part of the collector so you can process more than 1 hit). This last collision check could be avoided completely when caching the contact information during bisection.

@mihe I'd like to have your opinion on this.

> Note that `scale` is not passed to this function, so if there is any I think we have a bug.

Yes, a `MotionParameters::from` whose scaling differs from the scaling that's actually applied to the body (through `JPH::ScaledShape`) is broken right now. I have [this really old branch](https://github.com/godot-jolt/godot-jolt/compare/master...mihe:godot-jolt:body-test-motion-scale) where I tried to address this, but it turned out to be messier than I expected and then it fell by the wayside.

Passing anything but the body's `global_transform` into `body_test_motion` (which you can't even do with `move_and_collide`/`move_and_slide`) is likely a very niche use-case though, which is why I haven't rushed to fix it.

> I find it dangerous that the code that bisects collision to get the safe and unsafe fraction uses a different condition for detecting a collision than the code that retreives the contact information.

Yes. This is a hack, and is the reason for long-standing issues like godot-jolt/godot-jolt#758. It was preceded by an even worse hack at one point, but a spirited contributor who had done a bunch of investigation into Godot's `move_and_slide` [suggested](https://github.com/godot-jolt/godot-jolt/discussions/812) I replace it with the lesser hack you see there.

Unfortunately it's been long enough now that I don't remember all the details, but that hack was meant to work around problems that we perceived `CharacterBody3D::_move_and_slide_grounded` to have at the time. More specifically it's related at least in part to this bit of code, meant to deal with acute corners:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4a919adccf8e398aceca75399c539078c54fe97f/scene/3d/physics/character_body_3d.cpp#L280-L298

If you flip the dot product check as you (and I guess #114611) suggested, and then also do the same thing in `_body_motion_cast`, then `CharacterBody3D::move_and_slide` will almost certainly end up with a prohibitive amount of ghost collisions as a result of that `stop_all_motion` code.

My vague takeaway at the time (which I don't how true it actually is) was that `CharacterBody3D::move_and_slide` did not appropriately separate the collision checks meant to detect its surroundings (if we're on a wall, floor, etc.) and the collision checks meant to be used for slides, which seemed to make it impossible to detect all contacts appropriately while also avoiding ghost collisions. So I opted for the option that resulted in less ghost collisions.

In other words, `move_and_collide` suffers because it's used within `move_and_slide`, so had to cater to its quirks, since it likely makes up the majority use of `move_and_collide`.

With that said, Godot Physics does not do this type of contact discarding, and still manages to sit somewhere inbetween Jolt-without-that-check and Jolt-with-that-check in terms of the amount of ghost collisions you get, which annoyed me greatly, and I've probably spent a solid week or two of my life just trying to figure out why, without coming up with a good answer. So it's possible that some discrepancy between the two `body_test_motion` implementations is to blame here as well.

So yes, I know that `direction.dot(normal)` check is highly questionable, and you're more than welcome to change it (and anything else in `body_test_motion`) however you want, but just be sure to thoroughly test for regressions in ghost collisions if you do. This character mover stuff is way too time-consuming for me to be able to dive back into it any time soon.

As for the actual reported issue here, I haven't looked at either of the MRPs, but the fact that things supposedly behave fine in `_physics_process` but not `_process` sets of alarm bells in my head, so would seem worth finding an explanation to before we change anything about `_body_test_motion`. Is it just because of a different/random delta time in some way?

It may not strictly be a _process() only bug.  I couldn't get the MRP to reproduce the issue that my game had, then I realized I was updating the player in the _process() (doing my own fixed update times, so variable dt shouldn't be an issue).

Ok, yeah, I just tested and it still happens in _physics_process() if the physics update rate is doubled to 120 instead of 60.  Seems it's just caused by small deltas in general.  That makes more sense.

My general thoughts on the issue are that we should make test_move / move_and_collide() as accurate as possible then adjust move_and_slide() to handle any extra collisions rather than trying to fake non-collisions to account for quirks in the move_and_slide logic.

In this particular case, wouldn't it make the most sense to do `if (direction.dot(normal) > 0.0)`?

Edit: Interesting, only `if (direction.dot(normal) >= CMP_EPSILON)` fixes the issue.  Checking for > 0.0 still has the same behavior.  I've also noticed a new issue after the change: in some areas, moving from a flat area to a ramp causes the player to get stuck.  Not sure if that's a bug in my logic or something with the physics not reporting collision properly.  I'll have to investigate further.

Edit2: After some investigation on the flat-to-slope issue after making the `if (direction.dot(normal) >= CMP_EPSILON)` change, it seems that the collision keeps returning the normal of the flat ground, and even though I redirect the velocity to have a 0 Y component, I keep getting collision with the ground and never the slope, so the velocity never redirects up the slope and the character gets stuck.  So, sadly, changing that one line is not a complete fix.

> My general thoughts on the issue are that we should make test_move / move_and_collide() as accurate as possible then adjust move_and_slide() to handle any extra collisions rather than trying to fake non-collisions to account for quirks in the move_and_slide logic.

I would agree with you. My original aspiration was to change/fix `move_and_slide` in some way, assuming I could prove that the problem wasn't with my Jolt implementation of `body_test_motion`, but changing anything related to this stuff is often a week-long ordeal (at least for me as a layman in this space) and more often than not results in frustrating regressions that end up making their way into people's projects.

Unless I get tasked to fix this for some work-related stuff then someone else is likely going to have to figure this out.

Ok, I think the fundamental problem might be this: `JoltQueryCollectorClosestMulti<JPH::CollideShapeCollector, 32> collector(p_max_collisions);`

We create a collector with the max collisions, usually 1, then we loop through that collector and discard stuff that we're not moving into.  The problem is, if we're wedged into multiple collision objects, we can have a case where we're moving out of or parallel to one collision and into the other, but we discard the first one, and don't return the collision that's needed (the one we're moving into).

Just for kicks, I tried  `JoltQueryCollectorClosestMulti<JPH::CollideShapeCollector, 32> collector(p_max_collisions + 2);` and that seems to have fixed my issue without introducing new problems (so far).  Not sure if there are going to be significant performance issues collecting extra collisions, though.  Ideally, we'd return the "strongest" collisions (the ones the movement is going into the most), but that would require some extra sorting overhead that might not be worth it.

> Just for kicks, I tried `JoltQueryCollectorClosestMulti<JPH::CollideShapeCollector, 32> collector(p_max_collisions + 2);` and that seems to have fixed my issue without introducing new problems (so far).

The more proper fix for this is in [this branch](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/master...jrouwe:godot:114605) that @jrouwe shared [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/114605#issuecomment-3764040803).

That moves the filtering logic to the collector itself, allowing it to return the closest contact(s) that wouldn't be discarded.

I've rebased that branch and stepped through it with the MRP. It still discards the ceiling collision because the normal is perpendicular but then continues to find the floor and returns a proper collision. Both MRPs in this issue don't fail anymore with this change.

> Both MRPs in this issue don't fail anymore with this change.

I was just in the process of making a proper PR out of it, since I was curious to see what it could look like with the filtering done in the cast step as well: #118155

As mentioned there, I have barely tested it all, but it does indeed seem to resolve the MRPs here.

I know I experimented with having the filtering done in both steps at one point, but I vaguely recall running into issues with it at the time. I'm pretty sure I never did the filtering through the collector though, so maybe that changes things.

While you were doing that, I was doing the [exact same thing](https://github.com/jrouwe/godot/tree/114605_v2) :) I've tested it against the MRP of #114605 and realized that this approach is fundamentally flawed. The reason for this is that the bisection is not done with the original shape but with a `JoltCustomMotionShape` which extends the original shape by the motion. Sticking to the names and colors of the original MRP of #114605: And indeed, when running that MRP the normals are inconsistent between `_body_motion_cast` and `_body_motion_collide` leading to a missed collision. I think my original [fix](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/master...jrouwe:godot:114605) fixes this issue in a way that shouldn't break any other behavior but leaves #114605 broken. I currently don't see how I could apply the same test in `_body_motion_cast`.

I was fully prepared for #118155 not fixing #114605. The filtering of any perpendicular contact normals during motion is sort of the (hacky) point of this filtering, to alleviate whatever problems I perceived `move_and_slide` to have, as talked about [above](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/117857#issuecomment-4170023799).

But your point still stands, the filtering is indeed problematic to have in the cast step for the reason you mentioned. I'll go ahead and remove it, which I guess makes that decorator approach of mine look quite clumsy as well.
If you want, I can also make a PR out of my branch. I think that's relatively clean.

> If you want, I can also make a PR out of my branch. I think that's relatively clean.

Not that you couldn't have changed this yourself, but I preferred to not have inline struct/class definitions in the `JoltPhysicsDirectSpaceState3D` methods, since we have all the other custom collectors in `jolt_query_collectors.h` already.

I threw in some other minor unrelated changes as well.

(You're of course listed as co-author on the commit as well, and were from the start.)

I'll try to mess with it next week and maybe see about creating a test scene with some of the problem cases.  `This is a deliberate divergence from the Godot Physics reference implementation` I wonder if adding that to the Godot physics would fix the character getting stuck on things. 😁  That was a huge problem that made the Godot physics basically unusable for me.

Just out of curiosity, why does the motion use bisection and CollideShape instead of using jolt's CastShape?  Does jolt do the same thing under the hood and this is just to grab additional info?  Curious how CastShape compares for reliability and performance.  I've noticed a lot of tunneling issues if I drop the physics to 30fps, and there are some pretty significant performance issues with 100+ characters moving around (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/93184).

That said, doing the early out in the JoltQueryCollector will likely save a lot in _body_motion_recover, as that's doing 4x32 max collision results, so this should be a solid improvement overall!

> It still discards the ceiling collision because the normal is perpendicular but then continues to find the floor and returns a proper collision.

This is actually the correct behavior.  Once the movement is redirected along the surface of a collision, I wouldn't expect it to collide again.  I'm not sure why changing the epsilon check to allow for collision results on movement parallel to the surface fixed the ground collision (as that wasn't parallel, but going toward the ground).  I guess because of the bisection using the JoltCustomMotionShape mentioned above?

> Just out of curiosity, why does the motion use bisection and CollideShape instead of using jolt's CastShape?

Because `PhysicsTestMotionResult3D` supports returning a "safe" and "unsafe" fraction, which doesn't really work with how Jolt (and likely other physics engines) implement its shape-casting, as it can't guarantee that the result is either of those two. You can read (and see) more about that here: jrouwe/JoltPhysics#450

There was [an attempt](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/70522) by Juan to move the Godot Physics implementation away from the binary search, but it seemed to have some problems, and I would imagine likely suffered from the same safe/unsafe fraction problem as Jolt's shape-casting.

> That said, doing the early out in the JoltQueryCollector will likely save a lot in _body_motion_recover, as that's doing 4x32 max collision results, so this should be a solid improvement overall!

#118155 has no impact on `_body_motion_recover`, it only impacts `_body_motion_collide`, which now gets this new specialized filtering collector. I wouldn't expect it to move the needle much in terms of performance though. We're doing more filter checks as a result of doing it in the collector, but potentially less `AddHit` calls to the base collector, so it could all be a wash in the end.

But yes, `body_test_motion` is not cheap.

>> It still discards the ceiling collision because the normal is perpendicular but then continues to find the floor and returns a proper collision.

> This is actually the correct behavior

Yes, this is indeed the correct behavior. Sorry if I made it seem that it was not.

> [@jitspoe](https://github.com/jitspoe) If you could thoroughly test [#118155](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/118155) with your own character controller, to make sure there are no regressions in terms of weird collision results, that would be a good first step to getting it merged I guess.

Seems good so far.
